final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest pathogenicity score (0.984); introducing a charged Asp at a conserved Gly in the catalytic region is a classic disruptive substitution likely to abolish activity.
Very high pathogenicity (0.953); removing a catalytic-region histidine via Ala substitution is likely to eliminate a key functional side chain.
Strong pathogenicity (0.801); loss of an acidic residue in the catalytic domain likely impairs catalysis or substrate/cofactor handling enough to abolish function.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is stable across the collected evidence; remaining uncertainty (AlphaMissense is a proxy, not a direct activity assay) would not be resolved by the available tools.

history.rationale: Cys193 lies in the conserved N-terminal catalytic/FAD-region motif DYFDICVAGYPKGH; removing the cysteine should disrupt catalytic geometry and/or local packing. Chosen as a strong loss-of-function candidate rather than a mild stability allele.
Cys in the putative catalytic/FAD-binding region (residues ~150-330); loss of a conserved Cys commonly abolishes activity. Awaiting annotation/MSA/phenotype evidence.
Pathogenicity 0.297 (benign class) and modest PLM tolerance argue against strong LOF.

rejection.reason: Pathogenicity 0.297 (benign class) and modest PLM tolerance argue against strong LOF.

history.rationale: Asp191 is in the same highly conserved catalytic motif immediately before Cys193; neutralizing an acidic residue here is likely to impair catalysis or FAD/substrate positioning.
Conserved Asp in catalytic domain; charge removal near the active site is a strong LOF hypothesis.
AlphaMissense only 0.375 (ambiguous); insufficient evidence for abolishing activity.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense only 0.375 (ambiguous); insufficient evidence for abolishing activity.

history.rationale: Gly196 is part of the tight CAGYPKG turn where backbone flexibility is likely essential; introducing a bulky charged Asp should strongly distort the active-site loop.
Gly-to-Asp in a likely tight-turn/conserved region; steric/charge clash is a plausible strong LOF mechanism.
Highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity (0.984); introducing a charged Asp at a conserved Gly in the catalytic domain is a classic disruptive LOF substitution.
Lys199 sits in the conserved GYPKGHPE segment and may contribute to cofactor/substrate electrostatics; alanine substitution removes a likely functional positive charge.
Conserved Lys cluster (191-201) suggests functional importance; alanine scan candidate.
Lowest pathogenicity (0.159, benign) plus highest PLM plausibility (0.281) indicate this mutation is well tolerated — wrong direction for LOF.

rejection.reason: Lowest pathogenicity (0.159, benign) plus highest PLM plausibility (0.281) indicate this mutation is well tolerated — wrong direction for LOF.

history.rationale: His201 is embedded in the predicted catalytic motif and histidines commonly serve acid/base or metal/cofactor roles; loss should markedly reduce activity.
His often catalytic/acid-base; removal likely impairs catalysis while folding is preserved.
Very high pathogenicity score (0.953); His in catalytic region, alanine removal likely abolishes activity.
Trp165 is in the GDQWEEEEG region likely contributing to hydrophobic packing near the FAD-binding catalytic core; removing the indole should destabilize the active fold.
Large aromatic removal may destabilize hydrophobic core; moderate LOF probability.
Moderate pathogenicity (0.665); large hydrophobic-to-Ala change is disruptive but MSA shows some tolerance for Ala (0.174).
Arg183 is conserved in the HIRSEFGD stretch preceding the catalytic cysteine loop and may orient cofactor or substrate; charge removal is expected to be deleterious.
Conserved Arg in catalytic region; plausible salt-bridge/substrate-binding role.
Pathogenicity 0.757 supports LOF; charged Arg removal in conserved region.
Asp210 follows the active-site motif in the EADLKHLKE region and may support catalytic electrostatics; alanine substitution should impair activity more than a conservative Asn change.
Backup acidic-residue perturbation in catalytic domain.
Strong pathogenicity (0.801); acidic residue in catalytic domain likely functionally important.
Tyr197 is in the CAGYPKG catalytic loop; Phe removes only the hydroxyl but may retain packing, making it a useful comparator likely to be less severe than charge/loop disruptions.
Tyr-to-Phe is conservative; unlikely to abolish activity, so it poorly matches a full LOF goal.

rejection.reason: Tyr-to-Phe is conservative; unlikely to abolish activity, so it poorly matches a full LOF goal.

history.rationale: Ala222 is the well-known C677T thermolability site; included as a benchmark reduced-function allele, but it is less likely than active-site disruptions to fully abolish MTHFR activity.
The common A222V polymorphism is thermolabile but retains partial activity and is homozygous-viable; insufficient for abolishing function.

rejection.reason: The common A222V polymorphism is thermolabile but retains partial activity and is homozygous-viable; insufficient for abolishing function.
